name: Add an isochronic pulse layer under an existing track: a sine (or noise) carrier played by one long MIDI note, amplitude-pulsed at a chosen rate (e.g. 4 Hz) with a smooth-step pulse shape and a 0–100% isochronic blend, faded in and out by gain automation, with the pulse rate automated (e.g. 15 Hz → 4 Hz → 15 Hz) using ~10 ms parameter smoothing, carrier tuned by reference (440/432) or a custom note-to-frequency map and verified with a tuner, then mixed barely audible
goal: Build the Mind Amend-style isochronic layer as its own track. A tone generator plays a sine carrier from MIDI; with beat frequency 0 it is just a plain sine. Pick the pulse rate (e.g. 4 Hz) and raise the isochronic blend from 0% (steady tone) through 50% to 100% (full on/off pulses); choose a smooth-step pulse shape for focused but soft pulses. An amplitude-pulsing (LFO/tremolo) device lets you pulse noise or any audio as well. Use one long MIDI note for an uninterrupted tone (chords also work and pulse together). Fade in over about 30 s and out over 30–60 s with gain automation. Automate the pulse rate with exact typed breakpoints (e.g. start 15 Hz, glide to 4 Hz, return to 15 Hz at the end) and set the device's parameter smoothing to its minimum (0.01 = 10 ms) for automation. Keep pulse rates low (the speaker suggests below ~100 Hz); carrier frequencies (e.g. 432 Hz reference tuning, or a custom mapping where a note equals 528 Hz) are a separate layer of choice; check the actual pitch with a tuner set to the same reference. Finally set the layer's level in the mixer so it sits barely audible under the music. Polyrhythm Studio: OscillatorNode → GainNode whose gain follows a pulse-shaped LFO at rate r(t) with a ramped automation curve.

source.title: How to Create Isochronic Tones in Ableton Live with Huon Studio
source.transcript_note: Two-person screen-share session; off-topic chat dropped; product UI mapped to generic tone generator + amplitude pulse.

prerequisites: DAW with a tone/isochronic generator or any synth + tremolo/LFO amplitude device, gain utility with automation, and a tuner, or Web Audio: OscillatorNode (sine) → GainNode; gain driven by a smoothed square/raised-cosine LFO whose frequency AudioParam is automated with linearRampToValueAtTime (implementation note)
An existing music track to sit under

inputs.name: carrier
inputs.description: Carrier pitch (MIDI note, or Hz via tuning reference/custom map)

inputs.name: pulse_rate
inputs.description: Pulse rate in Hz (e.g. 4) or an automation curve (15 → 4 → 15 Hz)

inputs.name: pulse_shape
inputs.description: Pulse shape (smooth step recommended in the video)

inputs.name: fades
inputs.description: Fade-in (~30 s) and fade-out (30–60 s) times

outputs.name: isochronic_layer
outputs.description: Pulsed carrier track with fades and rate automation

outputs.name: mix_level
outputs.description: Final layer level relative to the music

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
No health or brainwave-entrainment claims are made by this skill; it is a sound-construction recipe only. Keep pulse/beat layers at low listening level.
Beat/pulse rate (a few Hz) and carrier frequency (hundreds of Hz) are different parameters; don't type a carrier value into the pulse rate.
With beat frequency 0 or blend 0% nothing is pulsed.
Set parameter smoothing to its minimum before automating rate, or fast changes lag.

Specific note-to-frequency maps (e.g. 'solfeggio' tunings) are user-supplied tuning tables; verify each pitch with a tuner rather than trusting the label. Product names mapped to generic tone generator + amplitude LFO.

steps.action: Create a MIDI track with the tone generator; set the device output low (about -20 dB) so the layer starts quiet.
steps.expect: A plain sine carrier at low level

steps.action: Program one long MIDI note (or loop a short note while designing; chords also work).
steps.expect: A steady carrier tone without interruptions

steps.action: Set the pulse rate (e.g. 4 Hz) and raise isochronic blend from 0% to 100%; choose a smooth-step pulse shape.
steps.expect: The tone turns on and off 4 times per second with soft edges

steps.action: Add a gain utility and automate a ~30 s fade-in at the start and a 30–60 s fade-out at the end.
steps.expect: The pulsed tone fades in and out gently

steps.action: Expose the pulse-rate parameter for automation, set parameter smoothing to 0.01 (10 ms), and draw breakpoints with typed values: 15 Hz at the start, 4 Hz in the middle section, back to 15 Hz at the end.
steps.expect: Pulses audibly slow from fast to 4 Hz and speed up again

steps.action: Optional carrier tuning: switch the tuning reference (440 → 432 Hz) or load a custom note-to-frequency map and find the note that gives the target frequency (e.g. 528 Hz); confirm with a tuner set to the same reference.
steps.expect: The tuner confirms the intended carrier pitch

steps.action: Set the track fader so the layer is barely audible under the music.
steps.expect: Pulses are perceptible but stay in the background

verification: At blend 0% the output is a steady sine; at 100% it is fully gated at the pulse rate.
Counting pulses over 1 s at the 4 Hz section gives about 4.
The rate automation lane shows 15 → 4 → 15 Hz with exact typed values.
A tuner shows the intended carrier frequency.
